question: Q-hswm-neural-substrate-causal-transfer
conjecture: A sealed typed packet (lessons + deltaW, sha256 + Merkle provenance) accumulated by donor agent A on corpus D_A causally improves frozen receiver B on disjoint heldout beyond every control: B-self lessons, placebo lessons, and A's raw log. Transfer is dark-knowledge only if B1's response distribution (including errors) correlates with A's more than B5's does.

arms.B5: B-self lessons (B generated from same experience)

secondary_discriminators.G: Acc(B1) - Acc(B5): cross-agent transfer surplus over self-generated lessons
secondary_discriminators.S: corr(B1 response distribution incl. errors, A distribution) - corr(B5 distribution, A distribution): dark-knowledge signature

common_chassis.disjoint_level: at least cross-split (3-tier: cross-task > cross-split > cross-domain)
common_chassis.leakage_audit: exact-query/entity/template overlap=0 + embedding near-dup threshold; leakage>0 voids run
common_chassis.scope_note: API-only B = input channel only; logit/activation channel (T2/T3) out of scope until local open-model pair

already_public_before_registration.note: Literature: naive memory transfer hurts (-1.6 to -8.6pt MATH500); abstracted/contrast-distilled memory transfers +12~15pt across families. No HSWM arm output measured.
already_public_before_registration.harness_provenance: foundation multi-agent-transfer-harness spec is filled by this gate (finding b1)

kill_conditions: f3_k1 G <= 0 -> claim 2 reduces to claim 1 (novel kill)
f3_k2 S <= 0 -> no dark-knowledge transfer; effect is generic priming - do not call it transfer
f3_k3 B1 <= max(B0,B2,B3) -> sub-claim dies; B1 <= B3 -> 'typed packet necessary' dies, demote to raw-data sharing effect (C1 precedent)
f3_k4 saturation (B0 >= 5/6) -> re-register with harder F2 family
pass_conditions: paired bootstrap LCB > 0 vs all controls
